prior_reason: The hold is closable exactly as the bucket description predicts: binisaya does have tinagpulo, and the tag-/tinag- distributive series is productive in Cebuano, so one corpus hit is rarity rather than doubt. The underlying defect is quantitative and provable from the card's own English: fact_en says tephra extends "tens of kilometers" and the Cebuano says "napulo ka mga kilometro" = ten kilometers, an order-of-magnitude understatement of the top of the range (and "ka mga" is ungrammatical after a numeral ligature, which is why I dropped mga to match the attested construction). Worth flagging upstream: this is a systematic MT flattening across the corpus, not a one-off, so other "tens of" cards are likely wrong the same way. emphasis_bis span "tephra" is preserved verbatim.
prior_evidence: binisaya.com/cebuano/tinagpulo: defined — "tenner (n.) — the cardinal number 10". binisaya.com/cebuano/tinagsa: "respective (adj.); one at a time (adv.)" — confirming the tinag- distributive series; binisaya parses tagpulo as tag- + pulo ("ten"), and Wikipedia's Cebuano numerals notes distributives are formed with the tag- prefix (tagpito "seven of each", tag-upat "four of each"). Corpus attests it for precisely this English: ffct-39675 "kalit nga lukso nga tinagpulo ka centimeters" (EN "a sudden jump of tens of centimeters"). The flattening pattern I want on record: dcard-04887 "napulo ka libo ka tuig" for EN "tens of thousands of years"; ffct-32789 "napulo ka milyon nga fungi" for EN "tens of millions of fungi" — so the old wording follows a corpus-wide error rather than defending itself.

fact_bis: Ang tephra kay mga tipik nga volcanic debris nga kusganong gipagawas sa atmosphere panahon sa explosive eruptions, ug kini makaabot ug napulo ka mga kilometro sa taas sa bulkan.

prior_reason: Another attestation-bucket close. The defect is a classic false-friend on the English word "fix": fact_en means chemical fixation of CO2, and the Cebuano rendered it with ayo = to repair/heal, so the child reads "the Calvin cycle can heal more carbon dioxide" — a false belief about what fixation is. kabit is dictionary-verified as attach/hook on, and the corpus's own carbon-fixation cards use exactly that root for the same reaction, so makakabit's single body attestation is rarity, not risk. emphasis_bis span "RuDP" is preserved verbatim.
prior_evidence: binisaya.com/cebuano/kabit: verb senses "hang on (to attach or append something)", "hitch (to hook or fasten)", "hook up (to connect or link)", "fix to; attach". Corpus carbon-fixation cards use kabit for this precise reaction: dcard-07990 "ang carbon dioxide sa hangin ikabit sa usa ka five-carbon molecule nga gitawag RuDP" (EN "carbon dioxide from the air is attached to a five-carbon molecule called RuDP") and dcard-03363 (EN "captured and attached to"). makakabit = 1 body, dcard-04146 "ang carbon nga adunay double bond makakabit lamang sa duha ka laing grupo" (EN "a carbon with a double bond can attach to only two other groups") — same chemical-attachment sense as here. Also ffct-30493 "kabiton ang habog nga mga aparador ... sa bungbong" (EN "fasten tall cabinets to the wall").

fact_bis: Kadaghanan sa mga PGAL molecules gamiton aron ma-regenerate ang RuDP, ang sinugdanan nga molecule, aron magpadayon ang pagtuyok sa Calvin cycle ug maka-ayo pa ug mas daghang carbon dioxide.
